canonical_seed.student_text:
A curling stone glides straight across nearly frictionless ice. For several seconds the horizontal forces on it add to zero. What should happen during that interval?
A. It must stop immediately.
B. It continues with constant velocity.
C. It speeds up because it is moving.
D. It turns even though the net force is zero.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A curling stone glides straight across nearly frictionless ice. For several seconds the horizontal forces on it add to zero. What should happen during that interval?

  1. It must stop immediately.
  2. It continues with constant velocity.
  3. It speeds up because it is moving.
  4. It turns even though the net force is zero.
choices: It speeds up because it is moving.
It turns even though the net force is zero.
canonical_seed.answer: B — It continues with constant velocity.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no change in velocity.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no change in velocity.

The motion record shows equal spacing every 0.5 s while the horizontal force model shows 18 N left and 18 N right. Are the motion and force evidence consistent? Explain.

Motion dots: •----•----•----•----•
Horizontal forces: 18 N ← [crate] → 18 N

canonical_seed.student_text:
A student says, “When the bus brakes, inertia pushes passengers forward.” Which correction is best?
A. Inertia is a forward force made by motion.
B. Inertia is a property of matter; passengers tend to keep their current velocity while the bus slows.
C. Inertia is the same as friction.
D. Inertia exists only while an object accelerates.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A student says, “When the bus brakes, inertia pushes passengers forward.” Which correction is best?

  1. Inertia is a forward force made by motion.
  2. Inertia is a property of matter; passengers tend to keep their current velocity while the bus slows.
  3. Inertia is the same as friction.
  4. Inertia exists only while an object accelerates.
choices: Inertia is a forward force made by motion.
Inertia is a property of matter; passengers tend to keep their current velocity while the bus slows.
Inertia is the same as friction.
Inertia exists only while an object accelerates.
canonical_seed.answer: B — Inertia is a property of matter; passengers tend to keep their current velocity while the bus slows.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Inertia is not a force; it is resistance to a change in motion.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Inertia is not a force; it is resistance to a change in motion.

Equal upward support and downward weight arrows.

canonical_seed.solution_text: A resting supported lamp has real forces that balance: support upward and weight downward.
